status: DRAFT, NOT LOCKED. Owner-approved acceptance-standard change (V0.13m-lite). Protocol lock and live inference NO GO.
supersedes: the V0.13j-V0.13l acceptance standard (lifecycle /4 acceptance), for the fail-closed persistence clauses only
ownerDecision: V0.13m-lite: Experimental Readiness Closure. DT13L-01 and DT13L-02 are fixed. For DT13L-03 and DT13L-04 the owner adopts a conservative fail-closed persistence policy instead of further double-fault recovery machinery. This is an explicit change to the previous acceptance standard; it does not relabel DT13L-03/04 as resolved.
blocking: Invalid evidence included in scientific analysis
Automatic retries or replacement draws that alter the protocol
nonblockingIfDisclosed: A genuine failed run classified INVALID
Loss of evidence during unrecoverable double failure, provided the run is rejected

failClosedPersistence.trigger: persistence or recovery fails and evidence cannot be reliably retained (including a failure while recovering a draw's result, or while building the failure report)
required: never seal it: the archive is INVALID (unusable)
never accept contradictory or insufficient evidence as a valid PARTIAL
report possible evidence loss (persistence-failure.json evidenceLoss and RecordingError.retainedEvidence)
preserve evidence where possible; never hide the inability to preserve it
failClosedPersistence.notBuilt: no additional nested recovery system for multiple simultaneous persistence failures

retentionSchema.evidenceLoss: null, or {possible: boolean, kind: string, detail: string, ...}: the disclosure that evidence may be incomplete or lost; unsealed failure evidence only, never part of a sealed archive

relationships.relation: retained model-response body versus the workflow parser's reading and the structured response metadata
relationships.rule: every retained response body (draw calls and call-journal returned outcomes) is independently reparsed under dreamteam.strict-json/v1. A body the permissive workflow parser (json.loads) reads must also be read by the strict parser (no duplicate key at any depth, including escaped-equivalent keys; no NaN/Infinity; no number overflowing to infinity; no trailing content; nesting within the parser's limit) and both readings must be identical under strict typed equality; the structured metadata (usage, servedModel, finishReason) must be the strict reading's fields. A body that neither parser reads (malformed, trailing content, empty) is an unparsed reply to the frozen workflow: it carries no structured metadata and contributes only as the workflow's own unparsed-reply handling. Exact response bytes are preserved; nothing model-visible changes.
relationships.onViolation: INVALID: the archive is excluded from analysis (an ambiguous response never contributes to COMPLETE or PARTIAL analysis)

relationships.relation: wall-clock halt versus the request-start guard, its message and the structured timestamps
relationships.rule: for a wall_clock halt, the guard fired at a monotonic reading e1 with e1 + request.timeoutSeconds > stop.wallClockSeconds; the message shows round(e2) for a later reading e2 >= e1; the evidence elapsedSeconds is a still later reading e3 >= e2. The verifier requires e3 + timeoutSeconds > wallClockSeconds and threshold - 0.5 < message seconds <= e3 + 0.5, where threshold = wallClockSeconds - timeoutSeconds. For every halt in an archive with SYSTEM_UTC timestamps, elapsedSeconds must agree with the structured journal timestamps within the tolerance: elapsedSeconds <= (stop transition - begin_preflight) + tolerance and elapsedSeconds >= (last event or call record preceding the halt - first event after begin_preflight) - tolerance.
relationships.toleranceReason: monotonic and UTC clocks are read separately; NTP slewing is bounded (500 ppm is 7.2 s over four hours); a larger clock step makes a genuine archive INVALID (availability limitation, disclosed)
relationships.syntheticTimestamps: archives with SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE timestamps are admissible only to an explicit fixture check (never to ordinary analysis); the timestamp agreement is not applied to them, the guard and message rules are
relationships.guard: the existing four-hour request-start guard (a request starts only if its whole timeout fits before the stop); no hard deadline is claimed

relationships.relation: draw_unrecorded aborted draw versus the workflow reconstructed from its retained call journal
relationships.rule: a draw_unrecorded draw is accepted in a PARTIAL only if replaying the frozen workflow over its retained journal outcomes stops at a dispatch or external boundary. If the retained outcomes complete the workflow, the draw may have completed and its result may have been lost (an unrecoverable double failure, or a forged archive): the archive is rejected, never accepted as PARTIAL.
relationships.onViolation: INVALID (analysis refused; possible evidence loss reported)
